name: UH-60 Black Hawk
variants: HH-60G Pave Hawk / HH-60W Jolly Green II (USAF)
summary: Twin-turbine medium utility helicopter that is the US Army's standard assault and medevac transport; USAF combat-rescue Pave Hawks and Jolly Green IIs and many civil firefighting conversions share the airframe.

wings: Four-blade main rotor with swept tips (wide-chord on the UH-60M)
Optional stub wings (ESSS) carrying external fuel tanks on long-range missions
engines: Two engines side by side on the cabin roof behind the rotor mast
Exhausts on each side of the roof, often with angled IR suppressors
fuselage: Long, low, flat-sided cabin with large sliding doors on both sides
Fixed main wheels well forward under the cockpit doors
Small fixed tailwheel at the very rear of the tail cone
Cockpit windscreen in a sloping, flat-paneled nose
tail: Four-blade tail rotor canted upward on the right side of the fin
Large all-moving horizontal stabilator low on the tail pylon
Long tail cone with a slight upward kink to the fin

tellTales: Tailwheel sits at the far end of the tail cone, a long way behind the main wheels
Tail rotor visibly tilted from vertical on a swept fin above a big low stabilator
Long, low cabin with two engines side by side on the roof and wheels, not skids

confusedWith.howToTell: The Army Black Hawk usually wears green or black, has a big sliding door on each side and lacks the Navy/Coast Guard hoist, folding-tail hinge, chin FLIR and sensor/weapon pylons; on the MH-60R and Jayhawk the tailwheel is also far forward under the cabin.
The S-92 is a much taller, boxier airliner-like helicopter with retractable gear in sponsons and a rear ramp; the Black Hawk is long, low and has fixed gear with a tailwheel.
The UH-1Y sits on skids with a narrow nose and an unswept fin; the Black Hawk has wheels, a tailwheel and a canted tail rotor over a low stabilator.

usCount.source: US Army fleet ~2,300 UH/HH-60 (Army FY2026 aviation data) + USAF HH-60G/W + ~450 FAA-registered civil UH-60/S-70 (FAA registry)
